name: Reading
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Reading, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Reading, MA: the Reading Common tree lighting with Santa on a firetruck, s'mores at fire pits, trolley rides and the Haverhill Line.
lede: Reading starts its Christmas season on the Sunday after Thanksgiving, when the chamber of commerce fills Reading Common with fire pits, carolers and a trolley, and Santa rides in on a firetruck to light the trees.
celebrates: Reading's holiday centerpiece is the Tree Lighting Celebration on Reading Common, run by the Reading-North Reading Chamber of Commerce. For an afternoon, the Common and nearby Woburn Street turn into a free community party. Families make s'mores at fire pits, drink hot chocolate poured by the Women's League of Reading, line up for face painting and photos with Santa, listen to carolers and ride a trolley around downtown. Local businesses sponsor each activity. At the end of the afternoon, Santa arrives on a firetruck and switches on the trees, and North Reading lights its own Common the same day.
lastyear: The 32nd annual Tree Lighting on Reading Common took place on Sunday, November 30, 2025, from 2 to 4:30 pm, ending when Santa arrived by firetruck to light the display. The Reading Post reported that the chamber sponsored event drew thousands of community members. Activities included s'mores, hayrides, jugglers, carolers, costumed characters and trolley rides, while the Women's League of Reading served hot chocolate and local restaurants offered snacks.
facts: The Reading tree lighting has run for more than three decades, with the 32nd edition held in 2025. The Reading-North Reading Chamber of Commerce says the Commons in Reading and North Reading are lit on the same day, the first Sunday after Thanksgiving, and that the events draw thousands of people. In Reading, Santa does not come by sleigh: he arrives on a firetruck near the end of the afternoon. The Women's League of Reading poured the hot chocolate in 2025 and is listed again on the chamber's current program.
trains: Reading sits on the MBTA Haverhill Line, which runs from Boston's North Station through Wakefield and Reading. Families coming from Boston or Wakefield can ride the line straight to Reading station. Neighboring Wakefield has two Haverhill Line stops, Wakefield and Greenwood. For a Christmas train ride, Edaville Family Theme Park in Carver runs its Holiday Express train through a Winter Wonderland of lights with Santa and Mrs. Claus. Check Edaville's site for the current year's nights and prices.

kidfact: On tree lighting day, Reading and North Reading both light their town Commons, and in Reading Santa arrives on a firetruck.
faq: When is the Reading tree lighting?

The Reading-North Reading Chamber of Commerce holds it on the first Sunday after Thanksgiving, in the afternoon, on Reading Common. Activities run for a couple of hours and end when Santa arrives by firetruck to light the trees. The chamber posts each year's schedule, sponsors and road closures on its events page.
Is the Reading tree lighting free?

Yes. The chamber describes the activities as free to the community, with local businesses sponsoring s'mores, hot chocolate, popcorn, face painting and pictures with Santa. The Women's League of Reading serves the hot chocolate, and a trolley offers rides around downtown from a stop on Woburn Street.
Can we take the train to Reading?

Yes. Reading has a stop on the MBTA Haverhill Line, which runs from North Station in Boston through Wakefield. During the tree lighting, Woburn Street is closed between Sanborn Street and Main Street, so check the chamber's road closure notes if you plan to drive.
Does North Reading have a tree lighting too?

Yes. The chamber says the Commons in Reading and North Reading are lit on the same day, the first Sunday after Thanksgiving. North Reading runs its own celebration on its town Common, so families can check the chamber's calendar for both programs.
